documents.text: IPPA - Winter School - Chiang Mai edition 2026 Login Create an account Forgot my password Winter School - Chiang Mai edition 2026 I want to apply Registration Home Seasonal School General Program Pobsook Chamchong's course Shunsaku Komatsuzaki's course Vishal Narain's course How to apply Fees Accommodation This edition will take place from November 30 to December 4, 2026. The call for applications is open until October 20! The Chiang Mai International Winter School on Public Policy will be organized from November 30th to December 4th and is co-organized with the Chiang Mai University School of Public Policy . The Winter School aims to provide the opportunity for Ph.D. students and early career researchers to advance their knowledge of Public Policy theories, concepts, and methodologies. Students will participate in workshops/case studies where they will be able to discuss their research projects and receive feedback from both their peers and acclaimed scholars of public policy. In 5 days, the Winter School offers its participants the opportunity to attend the following activities: Lectures from different International scholars on specific public policy approaches, concepts, and theories; Course on a particular issue given by an International scholar, according to students' preferences; Workshop sessions together with your group, giving the students the option to present their work to the group, and have their topic discussed by their peers and the professors or to participate in case studies. The call for applications is open until October 20! ADB Young Professionals Program (YPP) | Asian Development Bank Skip to main content Careers at ADB Step into a job that uplifts lives for millions across Asia and the Pacific. Work with us to solve the region’s complex challenges and deliver development solutions that support sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth. Make Your Move. Home Opportunities Current Opportunities Opportunities Highlights ADB Recruitment Process What We Offer What We Offer Life at ADB Expatriate Spouse Connect Program ADB Staff Association Talent Programs Young Professionals Program Internship Program Japan Scholarship Program Visiting Fellow Program FAQs Contacts ADB Young Professionals Program Build on your training and experience early on in your career with our structured talent management program. Designed to expand your potential, this program provides a foundation for a challenging and rewarding career in an international development environment. Be Key to Our ADB Strategy 2030 As a Young Professional, your growth with us is vital to how we will help building a prosperous, inclusive, resilient, and sustainable Asia and the Pacific. At ADB, we see you as a potential future leader and you will progress through: Fixed 3-year term appointment Start with an initial placement in an operations or operations support role in the ADB headquarters in Manila, Philippines. This initial assignment offers hands-on experience and exposure to our core operations, policies, and procedures, equipping you with the knowledge and insights to thrive and grow within the organization. Rotational assignment After 18 months, you will transition to a rotational assignment in another area of ADB. This will be aligned with both your career interests and our organizational needs, allowing you to grow your professional experience and deepen your subject matter expertise. It’s a valuable opportunity to advance professionally while contributing in a new and meaningful context within ADB. Muti-faceted development opportunities You will get to participate in a wide spectrum of activities, from facts-finding missions to policy studies and project executions. You’ll also be part of our Young Professional mentorship program, where our experienced technical international staff, many of whom began their careers as Young Professionals, will provide guidance and support that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Eligibility Application and Selection Current Opportunities Check Your Eligibility To be eligible for the ADB Young Professionals Program, you must: Be a national of an ADB member country. Be 32 years old and below. Hold at least a first-level university degree with proven academic track record in a field relevant to the job role. Have at least three years of work experience relevant to ADB. Be passionate and committed to development work. Be a keen and agile learner with strong interpersonal skills. Have excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Application and Selection Apply in early September when the application process opens. Visit the “Current Opportunities” tab to explore available positions. Sign up for the ADB Job Alerts to stay in the loop of new postings. Prepare for a multi-stage selection process if you are shortlisted. This includes an online assessment followed by a video interview where you record answers to pre-set questions in your own time. If you progress past this stage, you will be invited to panel interviews that take place between December and February. Check your application status through the application site here. Our HR team will also be in touch through email. Frequently Asked Questions Is the age requirement flexible? For the ADB Young Professionals Program, only applicants 32 years old and below will be considered. I have less than three years of work experience. Should I apply? You need to have a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience to be considered for the ADB Young Professionals Program, including internships. I applied to the ADB Young Professionals Program before. Can I apply again? Yes, you can apply again regardless of how far you have progressed in the application process previously, if you meet the eligibility requirements. What is the typical Young Professional progression? Young Professionals are international staff recruited at grade YP1. After the first 12 months probationary period, confirmed Young Professionals will be promoted to grade YP2. A Young Professional’s promotion to Grade TI1 occurs upon absorption into an assigned position. What is the curriculum of the ADB Young Professional Program? You will start your term with an 18-month initial assignment to either a solutions department (such as Climate, Thematic, or Private Sector Operations Department) or a major non-operational department in HQ (such as Economic Research and Development Impact Department (ERDI) or Office of Markets Development and Private Partnership (OMDP). Once you complete your assignment and are cleared for rotation, you will be assigned to another area. Ready for You Sign up for ADB Job Alerts to be notified when application opens. Contact For questions related to the ADB Young Professionals Program E-mail More Talent Programs Internship Project-oriented learning experience for graduate students through research assignments based on current operational needs. Scholarship Post-graduate scholarship for studies in economics, management, science and technology, and other development-related fields. Visiting Fellow Sharing opportunity for researchers and academics with ongoing or recently completed economic research at the ADB headquarters in Manila.
